about: A mechanical-mount benchmark entry (G25, held-out) in dev.json format. Tier 4 = a real product: bought-in parts placed from a catalogue (pipe, 2020 extrusion, M4 and M5 bolts, M4 nuts, T-nuts), a two-piece split clamp with a closing gap and captive nuts, and fit, preload and access requirements judged as interference and clearance checks against reference models and keep-out volumes. L1 ids match requirements.md next to this file, which holds the L2/L3 tree, the reference models, the assumptions and the traceability. Numbers that are not in the plan brief come from requirements.md section 3. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text, requirements, design_rules.json generic values and part.json catalogue data.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (stability, connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the part in, sweep a tool, load path)

requests.title: PVC pipe clamp to 2020 profile
requests.request: A clamp holds a 32 mm outside diameter PVC pipe to the face of a 2020 aluminium extrusion. The pipe runs parallel to the extrusion, with its axis 18 to 30 mm out from the face the clamp is mounted on (the extrusion is 100 mm long and I treat the pipe as a solid rod for the design). The clamp is a two-piece strap: a saddle with a back plate, and a cap, printed separately and joined by two M4 bolts that thread into captive hex nuts. The clamp bore is 32.3 mm so that the bolts close a 0.5 mm gap between the two pieces and squeeze the pipe. The back plate takes two M5 bolts into drop-in T-nuts in the slot of that extrusion face. It is printed on an FDM printer in PLA or PETG without supports, no bigger than 80 mm along the extrusion, 70 mm across it and 60 mm out from its face, and I need to reach every bolt with a hex key.
requests.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: pipe parallel to the extrusion (A1); the extrusion length 100 mm and the pipe as a solid rod (A2, A3); the M5 bolts use drop-in T-nuts (A4); FDM, PLA or PETG, no supports, hex-key access (A8, A9).

l1.text: The design shall place, from the parts catalogue, the 32 mm pipe, the 100 mm 2020 extrusion, two M5 T-nuts, two M5 bolts, two M4 bolts and two M4 nuts, with the pipe axis parallel to the extrusion axis and 18 to 30 mm out from the face the clamp is mounted on, with no two parts colliding, and shall declare that layout.
The clamp shall grip the 32 mm pipe in a round bore of 32.3 mm diameter, concentric with the declared pipe axis, with 20 to 40 mm of grip length.

The clamp shall be two separate printed bodies, a saddle that carries the back plate and a cap, that meet at a split plane through the bore axis, with a gap of 0.5 mm between their split faces as delivered.

Two M4 bolts shall pass through plain holes in the cap into two M4 hex nuts held captive in pockets in the saddle, one on each side of the pipe (axes 21.3 to 30 mm from the pipe axis, equal on both sides within 0.5 mm, the tip standing 0 to 3 mm past the nut), and the closed clamp shall be able to bring the cap fully down onto the saddle.
When the 0.5 mm gap is closed the bore shall squeeze the pipe: the span of the closed bore across the clamp direction shall be 31.8 mm, which is 0.2 mm less than the pipe.

The saddle's back plate shall lie flat on the extrusion's face, inside the 100 mm length (at least 5 mm from each end, plate 4 to 8 mm thick, at least 600 mm² on the face), with no printed material entering the extrusion or its slot.

The back plate shall take two M5 bolts on the slot centreline, 40 to 70 mm apart and at least 10 mm from the ends, into two drop-in T-nuts in the 2020 slot, each bolt long enough to engage its nut and short enough to clear the slot floor.

With the pipe in place, nothing printed shall touch the pipe except at the bore (everything else at least 0.5 mm away), and the pipe shall clear the extrusion, the M5 bolt heads and the plate by at least 0.5 mm.

Every bolt shall be reachable with a hex key along its axis, and the clamp shall go together in this order: saddle bolted to the extrusion, nuts dropped in, pipe laid into the saddle, cap fitted and bolted.

The material round the bore, the nut pockets and the bolt holes shall be thick enough to carry the bolt load: at least 3.0 mm round the bore, 1.5 mm round each pocket, 2.0 mm between an M4 hole and the bore and 3.0 mm between an M5 hole and the plate edge.

The saddle and the cap shall each be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports, in the print orientation the design states (no overhang steeper than 45° from vertical, no bridge over 15 mm).
The clamp as delivered shall measure at most 80 mm along the extrusion, 70 mm across it and 60 mm out from the extrusion face.

The design shall be delivered as a saddle STL and a cap STL (relaxed pose, extrusion frame, mm), the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout, the print orientations and the agent's own clearance report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.
